correctness.rationale: For f weakly increasing on [n], each semigroup inverse g must select one image point in each of f's r interval kernel blocks, and each cut separating g-fibers must lie between adjacent images b_i,b_(i+1) of f; conversely these independent choices satisfy both fgf=f and gfg=g. This establishes |V(f)|=product(a_i)*product(b_(i+1)-b_i). Balancing positive compositions gives the rank maximum B(n,r)B(n-1,r-1). A separate integer-break argument handles the coupled r/r-1 partition maxima and equality cases in each n mod 3, with small n separately. The two weighted generating-function coefficients give (binom(n+r-1,2r-1))^2 for ordered rank-r inverse pairs; rank one and empty products are included. Independently computed BOTH inverse equations directly on all weakly increasing transformations for n=1..6 and reproduced (M_n,E_n)=(1,1),(2,2),(4,2),(12,1),(24,2),(48,2), and ordered-pair totals 1,5,26,153,931,5794. These finite tests are only corroboration for the unrestricted n proof.
